brief: A hot September flash PMI (composite 58.4, services 58.7, manufacturing 57.0, all above survey and prior) points to GDP growth near 4% for 3Q, above JPM's own upgraded 3.5% forecast, but input cost inflation posted its largest monthly rise since 2020. JPM reads this as evidence the market had been underpricing terminal Fed funds levels, and it drove a bond-yield selloff: the 5Y auction tailed 3.2bp on weak demand, the 5Y yield broke the 5% technical level, and equities sold off (SPX -0.7%, NDX -1.1%). Separately, Iran's UN rhetoric hardened (demands unchanged, no limits on peaceful nuclear technology) while Brent broke back above $100 (+4.6% to $103.59); JPM lays out three Middle East scenarios (deal, no-deal/no-escalation, no-deal/escalation) with different rate and equity outcomes, and says an escalation could cut equities 2-3%. Futures positioning stays cautious even after a rebound (global equity net positioning at the 9th percentile), while OAT positioning fell for a second week, less than Bunds, showing reduced willingness to press OATs. JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral, keeps its core +Tech vs. -RTY trade, and would turn bullish on lower oil/yields, bearish on signs the consumer or AI capex is breaking.
